title: UniCA: Unified Covariate Adaptation for Time Series
one_liner: Frozen time series models can absorb extra information (images, text, categories) by learning lightweight adapters that homogenize diverse data into a common language.
lead: Time series foundation models (large pretrained models on billions of time-series examples) excel at forecasting using pure numbers, but cannot read images or text. When you want to forecast electricity demand using both past prices (numbers) and weather photos (images), you are stuck: the model cannot read the photos. UniCA solves this by adding lightweight "translation" modules that convert photos, text, and categories into the same number-series language the model already speaks, then wires them in at the right moments.

problem.h2: The frozen model cannot see extra data types
paras: Time series foundation models are trained on vast amounts of pure numeric time series. Once trained, they are frozen (you do not retrain the whole model because it is huge and expensive). But real forecasting tasks almost always have extra information: stock forecasts need sentiment from text, power grids need weather photos, sales forecasts need holiday categories. You cannot use that information because the frozen model does not know how to read it.

A beginner might try one of two things, both of which fail. First: throw away the frozen model and retrain a new one from scratch on the new mixed data. This ruins the generalization the pretraining gave you and needs huge budgets. Second: retrain the frozen model on the new data. Same problem; you erase the pretraining, and the model forgets how to handle new domains it saw only during pretraining. So you are trapped: you cannot use the extra data without destroying what made the model good.

callout.html: A frozen model trained on numbers alone cannot read photos, text, or categories without retraining and losing generalization.

steps.text: Photos go through a CNN, text through a transformer, categories through an embedding layer; each outputs a list of numbers.
All encoders output the same length, so now all extra data speaks the same number-language as the time series.
Mix the encoded extra data with the time series numbers using gated addition, enriching the input before the model's encoder sees it.
The frozen time series encoder runs on the enriched numbers, capturing how the data and covariates evolve together.
Use the future covariates (known at forecast time) and weighted selection to pick and mix the most relevant future signals into the forecast.

paras: UniCA modifies the input and output of a frozen time series model by inserting two small trainable adapter modules: a pre-fusion module before the model's encoder, and a post-fusion module after it. The frozen time series backbone never changes. Only the adapters learn.

hidden.h2: The fusion gate: gating how much covariate information enters
hidden.name: Fusion gate weights
paras: UniCA uses a gated linear unit (a function that learns when to let information pass through, like a adjustable valve). Each gated fusion decides how much of the extra covariate information should actually be mixed in at that step. This gate is learnable: during training, it discovers how much to trust the photos, text, or categories at each moment. Without gating, you might contaminate the time series signal with irrelevant covariates.

The gate is estimated by learning which historical examples had high or low impact from the covariates. If past patterns show that text sentiment matters but photos do not, the gate learns to pass text and block photos. The paper does not explicitly name this, but it is the core of why the fusion works: selective trust.

heat.caption: Each gate controls how much each covariate type flows in; darker means higher gate value, more signal passes through.

reads.html: The gate is a learned on-off valve that passes covariate signals when useful and blocks them when not.
The gated linear unit (GLU) layer in Equation 5 learns gate weights that modulate the fused representation, selecting relevant covariate information.

mechanism.h2: Why it works: two-stage covariate injection
paras: The genius move is WHERE the adapters attach. The time series encoder is a temporal feature extractor: it looks at how the numbers change over time and finds patterns (trends, cycles, anomalies). If you dump raw covariate data into the encoder before it has looked at the time series signal, you contaminate the process. If you apply covariates only at the end, the model has already extracted temporal features and cannot blend them deeply. UniCA solves this with two stages.

First, the pre-fusion module adds encoded covariates BEFORE the encoder runs, enriching the input numbers with external context. The encoder then learns how this external context interacts with the time series evolution together. Second, the post-fusion module applies future covariates AFTER the encoder has extracted temporal patterns. Because you know future covariates at forecast time (a photo of tomorrow's weather is available today), this module uses weighted selection to pick which future signals matter most for each forecast time step. The key: both modules keep the pretrained model frozen. You are only training lightweight adapters, not relearning the entire temporal extraction from scratch.

stages.s: Encode each covariate type (CNN for images, transformer for text, embedding for categories)
Pre-fuse: gated addition of encoded covariates to time series numbers
Frozen encoder: extract temporal patterns from enriched numbers
Post-fuse: weighted selection picks future covariates
Forecast incorporating time series + all covariate types

math.words: Fused representation equals the original token plus the gated covariate signal: pre-fused token equals token plus gated linear unit applied to the concatenated tokenized covariate and time series.
symbols: gated linear unit: learned valve that decides how much to add
stick two lists of numbers together

worked.title: A tiny worked example
lines: Original time series token Z: [0.5, -0.2, 0.8] (three numbers capturing price, volume, trend).
Encoded weather photo C: [0.1, 0.3, -0.1] (three numbers from the image encoder).
GLU computes: learned weights multiply each number, then a sigmoid gate decides the on-off fraction. Suppose gate output is [0.8, 0.2, 0.9] on the covariate part.
The frozen encoder now reads [0.58, -0.14, 0.71] and extracts temporal patterns that absorbed the weather info.

math.note: The gated addition preserves the frozen model's learned knowledge while slowly mixing in the new covariate signals, preventing contamination.

items.html: If the covariate encoder (e.g., the image CNN) was trained on a different set of images than your task data, the encoded representations may be misleading, because the encoder itself may overfit to the pretraining domain. Solution: use a general-purpose pretrained image model or fine-tune the encoder lightly.

items.b: Future covariate leakage at train time.
items.html: The post-fusion module uses future covariates (weather photo of tomorrow). At training time, you have both past and future. If the gate learns to trust only the future, it will not work at test time when future covariates are predictions, not ground truth. Solution: during training, sometimes hide future covariates or add noise to teach the model to hedge.

Some covariates may be irrelevant for some tasks. If text sentiment does not predict your target, the adapter may overfit to noisy patterns or waste capacity, because the model is forced to find patterns in meaningless signals. Solution: validate which covariate types help on a separate tuning set, because only including truly informative covariates prevents the gate from learning to falsely trust noisy signals, which would mix misleading hints into the pretrained model's decisions.
Keep the pretrained backbone frozen and only train the adapters. Validate covariate relevance and encoder quality before deployment. Use weighted selection to learn task-specific gate patterns.

demo.h2: What a runnable demo should prove
paras: Build a small time series forecast task (electricity demand over 30 days) with both numeric features (temperature in Celsius) and a categorical covariate (hour of day: morning / afternoon / evening) and a text covariate (sentiment from a news headline). Train a frozen pretrained time series model baseline (no covariates). Train UniCA with all three covariate types. Measure forecast accuracy (how close the predicted demand is to the actual demand) on a held-out test set.
demo.closing: The demo must show that UniCA's forecast outperforms the frozen model without covariates, proving that the adapters successfully translate heterogeneous data into useful signals the frozen model can absorb, because the added information arrives at the right moments (pre and post-fusion) where it shapes predictions.
